No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Fintiri Declares Adamawa For Tinubu As PBAT Movement Unveils Buses by Attah Anthony 6 seconds ago in North East , 2023 Elections , News , Politics Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Adamawa State Governor, Ahmadu Fintiri, has declared support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, describing the state as an “Asiwaju state”, as the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement unveiled campaign buses for coordinators in 14 states ahead of the 2027 general elections. Fintiri made the declaration at the campaign launch of the movement, which also featured the handover of additional vehicles to strengthen grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election bid. The vehicles are expected to facilitate community outreach and campaign activities across local government areas as the movement expands its mobilisation network ahead of the 2027 elections. Speaking at the handover ceremony, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Adekanbi Asuku, urged the beneficiaries to strengthen collaboration and intensify grassroots engagement in support of the President’s re-election. Asuku said the deployment was part of efforts to empower state coordinators to reach more communities and communicate the achievements of the Tinubu administration and its Renewed Hope Agenda. The movement said it would expand its operations to additional states through consultations and sustained outreach, with state and local government structures serving as the backbone of its door-to-door mobilisation strategy. The PBAT Door-to-Door Movement is seeking to consolidate its grassroots presence as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general elections.
